Dissertation 2026-Data Analysis

2026-06-16

# Install all required packages (run once)
install.packages("tidyverse")      # data manipulation and ggplot2 for visualisations
install.packages("janitor")        # clean_names()
install.packages("psych")          # EFA, Cronbach's alpha
install.packages("car")            # VIF
install.packages("lmtest")         # Breusch-Pagan
install.packages("boot")           # bootstrapping
install.packages("gt")             # tables
install.packages("gtsummary")      # descriptives table
install.packages("effectsize")     # eta squared
install.packages("moments")        # skewness and kurtosis
install.packages("ggplot2")        # visualisations (included in tidyverse)

Loading required packages

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(psych)
library(car)
library(lmtest)
library(boot)
library(gt)
library(gtsummary)
library(effectsize)
library(moments)
library (ez)

Load file

df <- read_csv("Dissertation/210.csv")

standardise column names and creating condition variables

df <- clean_names(df)

df <- df %>%
  mutate(condition = case_when(
    !is.na(mpq7) ~ "MP",
    !is.na(emq7) ~ "EM",
    !is.na(arq7) ~ "AR",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

table(df$condition)
## 
## AR EM MP 
## 70 69 71

Coalescing to create a single shared column to compare across conditions

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    ai_use_1 = coalesce(mpq2_1, emq2_1, arq2_1),
    ai_use_2 = coalesce(mpq2_2, emq2_2, arq2_2),
    ai_use_3 = coalesce(mpq2_3, emq2_3, arq2_3),
    ai_use_4 = coalesce(mpq2_4, emq2_4, arq2_4),
    ai_use_5 = coalesce(mpq2_5, emq2_5, arq2_5),
    ai_use_6 = coalesce(mpq2_6, emq2_6, arq2_6),
    ai_disclosure_1 = coalesce(mpq3_1, emq3_1, arq3_1),
    ai_disclosure_2 = coalesce(mpq3_2, emq3_2, arq3_2),
    ai_disclosure_3 = coalesce(mpq3_3, emq3_3, arq3_3),
    ai_disclosure_4 = coalesce(mpq3_4, emq3_4, arq3_4),
    ai_disclosure_5 = coalesce(mpq3_5, emq3_5, arq3_5),
    ai_disclosure_6 = coalesce(mpq3_6, emq3_6, arq3_6),
    mancheck1_1 = coalesce(mpq4_1, emq4_1, arq4_1),
    mancheck1_2 = coalesce(mpq4_2, emq4_2, arq4_2),
    mancheck1_3 = coalesce(mpq4_3, emq4_3, arq4_3),
    mancheck2_1 = coalesce(mpq5_1, emq5_1, arq5_1),
    mancheck2_2 = coalesce(mpq5_2, emq5_2, arq5_2),
    mancheck2_3 = coalesce(mpq5_3, emq5_3, arq5_3)
  )

Recoding AI diclosure (scale of 1-6 to 1-5) by collapting 1 and 2 (I do not use AI and Most Unlikely)

recode_disclosure <- function(x) {
  case_when(
    x == 1 ~ 1,
    x == 2 ~ 1,
    x == 3 ~ 2,
    x == 4 ~ 3,
    x == 5 ~ 4,
    x == 6 ~ 5,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )
}

df <- df %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("ai_disclosure"), recode_disclosure))

# NA check - should all be 0
df %>%
  select(starts_with("ai_use"), starts_with("ai_disclosure"),
         starts_with("mancheck")) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.))))

Checking Missing Data (across all columns)

missing_summary <- df %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_missing") %>%
  filter(n_missing > 0) %>%
  mutate(percent_missing = round(n_missing / nrow(df) * 100, 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_missing))

Comprehension Check

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    comprehension_fail = case_when(
      condition == "MP" & mpq7 != 2 ~ TRUE,
      condition == "EM" & emq7 != 2 ~ TRUE,
      condition == "AR" & arq7 != 2 ~ TRUE,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  )

# how many failed by condition
df %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(n_failed = sum(comprehension_fail))
## # A tibble: 3 × 2
##   condition n_failed
##   <chr>        <int>
## 1 AR               3
## 2 EM               2
## 3 MP               4
#primary sample excluding comprehension failures
df_primary <- df %>%
  filter(comprehension_fail == FALSE)

#sample size and condition counts
cat("Primary sample size:", nrow(df_primary), "\n")
## Primary sample size: 201
table(df_primary$condition)
## 
## AR EM MP 
## 67 67 67

Comprehension check and exclusion - n = 201, 9 fails (excluded)

Who failed comprehension check?

#comprehension failures are disproportionately non-native English speakers?
df %>%
  mutate(native_english = ifelse(b2q4 == 1, "Native", "Non-native")) %>%
  group_by(comprehension_fail, native_english) %>%
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = native_english, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(total = Native + `Non-native`,
         pct_non_native = round(`Non-native` / total * 100, 1))
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by comprehension_fail and native_english.

Inconsistency check

# Flag items where ai_use = 1 (Highly Unlikely) but ai_disclosure >= 3
df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(
    inconsistent_1 = ai_use_1 == 1 & ai_disclosure_1 >= 3,
    inconsistent_2 = ai_use_2 == 1 & ai_disclosure_2 >= 3,
    inconsistent_3 = ai_use_3 == 1 & ai_disclosure_3 >= 3,
    inconsistent_4 = ai_use_4 == 1 & ai_disclosure_4 >= 3,
    inconsistent_5 = ai_use_5 == 1 & ai_disclosure_5 >= 3,
    inconsistent_6 = ai_use_6 == 1 & ai_disclosure_6 >= 3,
    n_inconsistent = inconsistent_1 + inconsistent_2 + inconsistent_3 +
                     inconsistent_4 + inconsistent_5 + inconsistent_6
  )

# Distribution of inconsistent items
table(df_primary$n_inconsistent)
## 
##   0   1   2   3   4   5 
## 174  11   8   4   2   2
# How many participants have at least one inconsistency
sum(df_primary$n_inconsistent > 0)
## [1] 27

183 no inconsistency, 11 inconsistent on 1 item and 8 inconsistent on 2 items.

recoding categorical variables

# Recode categorical variables (demographics)
df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(
    level_of_study = case_when(
      b2q1 == 1 ~ "Undergraduate",
      b2q1 == 2 ~ "Postgraduate Taught",
      b2q1 == 3 ~ "Postgraduate Research",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    field_of_study = case_when(
      b2q2 == 1 ~ "Humanities and Arts",
      b2q2 == 2 ~ "Social Sciences",
      b2q2 == 3 ~ "Politics, Law and International Relations",
      b2q2 == 4 ~ "Economics and Business",
      b2q2 == 5 ~ "STEM",
      b2q2 == 6 ~ "Other",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    gender = case_when(
      b2q3 == 1 ~ "Female",
      b2q3 == 2 ~ "Male",
      b2q3 == 3 ~ "Non-Binary",
      b2q3 == 4 ~ "Prefer not to say",
      b2q3 == 5 ~ "Other",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    english_proficiency_label = case_when(
      b2q4 == 1 ~ "Native speaker",
      b2q4 == 2 ~ "Fluent non-native speaker",
      b2q4 == 3 ~ "Intermediate",
      b2q4 == 4 ~ "Basic",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    ai_frequency = case_when(
      b2q8 == 1 ~ "Never",
      b2q8 == 2 ~ "Rarely",
      b2q8 == 3 ~ "Sometimes",
      b2q8 == 4 ~ "Often",
      b2q8 == 5 ~ "Very often",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    recruitment = case_when(
      b2q9 == 1 ~ "Prolific",
      b2q9 == 2 ~ "Social media",
      b2q9 == 3 ~ "WhatsApp or messaging app",
      b2q9 == 4 ~ "Reddit",
      b2q9 == 5 ~ "Personal Networks",
      b2q9 == 6 ~ "Other",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

Descriptives Table

df_primary %>%
  tbl_summary(
    include = c(level_of_study, field_of_study, gender,

      level_of_study            ~ "Level of Study",

      gender                    ~ "Gender",
      english_proficiency_label ~ "English Proficiency",
      ai_frequency              ~ "AI Use Frequency",

Country standardisation + Overlap

# b2q6 = country of adolescence (used for UAI mapping)
# b2q7 = country of citizenship (descriptive only)

# Standardise country of adolescence (b2q6)
df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(country_adolescence = case_when(
    grepl("england|uk|united kingdom|scotland|wales|britain|britian",
          tolower(b2q6)) ~ "United Kingdom",
    tolower(b2q6) == "austria"                        ~ "Austria",
    tolower(b2q6) == "bahrain"                        ~ "Bahrain",
    tolower(b2q6) == "bangladesh"                     ~ "Bangladesh",
    tolower(b2q6) == "canada"                         ~ "Canada",
    tolower(b2q6) == "china"                          ~ "China",
    tolower(b2q6) == "colombia"                       ~ "Colombia",
    tolower(b2q6) == "ecuador"                        ~ "Ecuador",
    tolower(b2q6) == "germany"                        ~ "Germany",
    tolower(b2q6) == "ghana"                          ~ "Ghana",
    tolower(b2q6) == "india"                          ~ "India",
    tolower(b2q6) == "indonesia"                      ~ "Indonesia",
    tolower(b2q6) == "ireland"                        ~ "Ireland",
    tolower(b2q6) == "italy"                          ~ "Italy",
    tolower(b2q6) == "jamaica"                        ~ "Jamaica",
    grepl("kenya", tolower(b2q6))                     ~ "Kenya",
    tolower(b2q6) == "latvia"                         ~ "Latvia",
    tolower(b2q6) == "malaysia"                       ~ "Malaysia",
    tolower(b2q6) == "nepal"                          ~ "Nepal",
    tolower(b2q6) == "nigeria"                        ~ "Nigeria",
    tolower(b2q6) == "north macedonia"                ~ "North Macedonia",
    tolower(b2q6) == "pakistan"                       ~ "Pakistan",
    tolower(b2q6) == "peru"                           ~ "Peru",
    tolower(b2q6) == "romania"                        ~ "Romania",
    tolower(b2q6) == "saudi arabia"                   ~ "Saudi Arabia",
    tolower(b2q6) == "serbia"                         ~ "Serbia",
    tolower(b2q6) == "south africa"                   ~ "South Africa",
    tolower(b2q6) == "south korea"                    ~ "South Korea",
    tolower(b2q6) == "spain"                          ~ "Spain",

    tolower(b2q6) == "qatar"                          ~ "Qatar",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

# Standardise country of citizenship (b2q7)
df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(country_citizenship = case_when(
    grepl("england|uk|united kingdom|scotland|wales|britain|britian|british",
          tolower(b2q7)) ~ "United Kingdom",
    grepl("kenya|kenyan", tolower(b2q7))              ~ "Kenya",
    grepl("nigeria|nigerian", tolower(b2q7))          ~ "Nigeria",
    grepl("india|indian", tolower(b2q7))              ~ "India",
    tolower(b2q7) == "austria"                        ~ "Austria",
    tolower(b2q7) == "bangladesh"                     ~ "Bangladesh",
    tolower(b2q7) == "canada"                         ~ "Canada",
    grepl("china|chian", tolower(b2q7))               ~ "China",
    tolower(b2q7) == "colombia"                       ~ "Colombia",
    tolower(b2q7) == "ecuador"                        ~ "Ecuador",
    grepl("german", tolower(b2q7))                    ~ "Germany",
    grepl("ireland|irelnd", tolower(b2q7))            ~ "Ireland",
    grepl("italy|ita", tolower(b2q7))                 ~ "Italy",
    tolower(b2q7) == "jamaica"                        ~ "Jamaica",
    tolower(b2q7) == "latvia"                         ~ "Latvia",
    tolower(b2q7) == "malaysia"                       ~ "Malaysia",
    tolower(b2q7) == "nepal"                          ~ "Nepal",
    tolower(b2q7) == "pakistan"                       ~ "Pakistan",
    tolower(b2q7) == "peru"                           ~ "Peru",
    tolower(b2q7) == "poland"                         ~ "Poland",
    tolower(b2q7) == "portugal"                       ~ "Portugal",
    tolower(b2q7) == "romania"                        ~ "Romania",
    tolower(b2q7) == "serbia"                         ~ "Serbia",
    tolower(b2q7) == "south africa"                   ~ "South Africa",
    tolower(b2q7) == "south korea"                    ~ "South Korea",
    tolower(b2q7) == "spain"                          ~ "Spain",
    tolower(b2q7) == "united states" | tolower(b2q7) == "usa" ~ "United States",
    tolower(b2q7) == "zimbabwe"                       ~ "Zimbabwe",
    tolower(b2q7) == "-" | tolower(b2q7) == "prefer not to mention" ~ NA_character_,
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

# Check NAs
cat("NAs in country_adolescence:", sum(is.na(df_primary$country_adolescence)), "\n")
## NAs in country_adolescence: 2
cat("NAs in country_citizenship:", sum(is.na(df_primary$country_citizenship)), "\n")
## NAs in country_citizenship: 4
# Overlap check
overlap <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(same_country = country_adolescence == country_citizenship) %>%
  summarise(
    same = sum(same_country, na.rm = TRUE),
    different = sum(!same_country, na.rm = TRUE),
    total = n()
  )
print(overlap)

Country of Adolescence descriptives table

uai_table <- df_primary %>%
  count(country_adolescence) %>%
  filter(!is.na(country_adolescence)) %>%
  mutate(uai = uai_scores[country_adolescence]) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  rename(Country = country_adolescence, N = n, UAI = uai)

uai_table %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table 3. Country of Adolescence and Hofstede UAI Scores (N = 199)") %>%
  cols_label(
    Country = "Country",
    N       = "N",
    UAI     = "UAI Score"
  ) %>%

As the scale items were adapted for this study, EFA is used to understand associations between all the factors. Parallel analysis is used to determine the number of factors for each scales. It compares eigenvalues from real data against random data of the same size and retains factors that explain more variance than chance.

# Select items
ai_use_items <- df_primary %>% select(starts_with("ai_use"))
ai_disclosure_items <- df_primary %>% select(starts_with("ai_disclosure"))

# Parallel analysis
fa.parallel(ai_use_items, fm = "pa", fa = "fa", 
            main = "Parallel Analysis - AI Use")

## Parallel analysis suggests that the number of factors =  3  and the number of components =  NA
fa.parallel(ai_disclosure_items, fm = "pa", fa = "fa", 
            main = "Parallel Analysis - AI Disclosure")

## Parallel analysis suggests that the number of factors =  3  and the number of components =  NA

Which items cluster together onto which factors, which then tells you whether your scale items are measuring one thing or multiple distinct dimensions.

# Principal axis factoring (fm = "pa") with oblimin rotation (oblique) allows factors to correlate, appropriate for psychological constructs. The cutoff = 0.3.

# AI Use - 3 factor solution (parallel analysis suggestion)
efa_ai_use_3 <- fa(ai_use_items, nfactors = 3, fm = "pa", rotate = "oblimin")
## maximum iteration exceeded
## Loading required namespace: GPArotation
print(efa_ai_use_3$loadings, cutoff = 0.3)
## 
## Loadings:
##          PA1    PA2    PA3   
## ai_use_1  0.621              
## ai_use_2  0.604              
## ai_use_3                0.896
## ai_use_4  0.423         0.427
## ai_use_5         0.930       
## ai_use_6  0.346  0.353       
## 
##                  PA1   PA2   PA3
## SS loadings    1.049 1.023 1.015
## Proportion Var 0.175 0.170 0.169
## Cumulative Var 0.175 0.345 0.514

RESULTS: Nearly equal variance across factors (17.5%, 17.0%, 16.9%) — no meaningful structure, Items 4 and 6 cross-load, Overall– 3-factor solution is not interpretable

# AI Use - 2 factor solution
efa_ai_use_2 <- fa(ai_use_items, nfactors = 2, fm = "pa", rotate = "oblimin")
## maximum iteration exceeded
## Warning in fac(r = r, nfactors = nfactors, n.obs = n.obs, rotate = rotate, : An
## ultra-Heywood case was detected.  Examine the results carefully
print(efa_ai_use_2$loadings, cutoff = 0.3)

## Loadings:

## ai_use_1  0.546       
## ai_use_2  0.715       
## ai_use_3         1.128
## ai_use_4  0.451       
## ai_use_5  0.488       
## ai_use_6  0.549       
## 
##                  PA1   PA2
## SS loadings    1.552 1.400
## Proportion Var 0.259 0.233
## Cumulative Var 0.259 0.492

Results: Heywood case confirmed — ai_use_3 loading at 1.128, unstable solution.

# AI Use - 1 factor solution
efa_ai_use_1 <- fa(ai_use_items, nfactors = 1, fm = "pa", rotate = "none")
print(efa_ai_use_1$loadings, cutoff = 0.3)

## Loadings:

## ai_use_2 0.600
## ai_use_3 0.657
## ai_use_4 0.657
## ai_use_5 0.658
## ai_use_6 0.455
##

## SS loadings    2.129
## Proportion Var 0.355

RESULT: Stable — all loadings 0.46–0.66, 35.5% variance explained, no warnings. 1-factor solution confirmed for ai_use

Factor loading tables

# Extract loadings for 1-factor ai_use
loadings_use <- as.data.frame(unclass(efa_ai_use_1$loadings)) %>%
  round(3) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Item") %>%
  mutate(
    Item = c("Brainstorming ideas and refining topic",
             "Conducting literature review",
             "Rewriting paragraphs or sentences",
             "Evaluating or assessing writing",
             "Writing parts of essay",
             "Summarising without reading source"),
    Scale = "AI Use"
  )
names(loadings_use)[2] <- "Factor 1"

# Replace small loadings with blank
loadings_use["Factor 1"] <- lapply(loadings_use["Factor 1"],
                                    function(x) ifelse(abs(x) < 0.3, "", x))

# Extract loadings for 2-factor ai_disclosure
loadings_disclosure <- as.data.frame(unclass(efa_ai_disclosure_2$loadings)) %>%
  round(3) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Item") %>%
  mutate(
    Item = c("Disclosing brainstorming ideas and refining topic",
             "Disclosing conducting literature review",
             "Disclosing rewriting paragraphs or sentences",
             "Disclosing evaluating or assessing writing",
             "Disclosing writing parts of essay",
             "Disclosing summarising without reading source"),
    Scale = "AI Disclosure"
  )
names(loadings_disclosure)[2:3] <- c("Factor 1", "Factor 2")

# Replace small loadings with blank
loadings_disclosure[c("Factor 1", "Factor 2")] <- lapply(
  loadings_disclosure[c("Factor 1", "Factor 2")],
  function(x) ifelse(abs(x) < 0.3, "", x))

# Print tables
loadings_use %>%
  select(Scale, Item, `Factor 1`) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table 4. EFA Factor Loadings - AI Use (1 factor)")

Scale Item Factor 1

loadings_disclosure %>%
  select(Scale, Item, `Factor 1`, `Factor 2`) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table 5. EFA Factor Loadings - AI Disclosure (2 factors)")
Table 5. EFA Factor Loadings - AI Disclosure (2 factors)
Scale Item Factor 1 Factor 2
AI Disclosure Disclosing brainstorming ideas and refining topic 0.742
AI Disclosure Disclosing conducting literature review 0.584
AI Disclosure Disclosing rewriting paragraphs or sentences 0.536 0.333
AI Disclosure Disclosing evaluating or assessing writing 0.588
AI Disclosure Disclosing writing parts of essay 0.934
AI Disclosure Disclosing summarising without reading source 0.683

AI disclosure shows a 2-factor structure - single composites for the primary analysis for parsimony. Future studies can explore these subscales.

Discussion - theoretical implications - disclosure intentions are not the same across all items, they cluster into two groups - group 1 (Rewriting paragraphs or sentences, writing parts of your essay and summarising without reading the source) & group 2 (Brainstorming and refining topic, Conducting literature review, Evaluating or assessing your writing). Participants respond differently to both, which suggests if they are confirmed, they could have implications on the design of policies. [Use Qual]

Composites

# Single composite score as mean of all 6 items for each scale
# Justified by 1-factor EFA solution and acceptable Cronbach's alpha

df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(
    ai_use_composite = rowMeans(select(., ai_use_1:ai_use_6), na.rm = TRUE),
    ai_disclosure_composite = rowMeans(select(., ai_disclosure_1:ai_disclosure_6), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

#distributions
summary(df_primary$ai_use_composite)

Assumptions

# Shapiro-Wilk test - tests whether data significantly deviates from normal distribution. If p > .05 = normality holds, p < .05 = normality violated. Q-Q plots provide visual confirmation

# Shapiro-Wilk tests
shapiro.test(df_primary$ai_use_composite)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  df_primary$ai_use_composite
## W = 0.9879, p-value = 0.08531
shapiro.test(df_primary$ai_disclosure_composite)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  df_primary$ai_disclosure_composite
## W = 0.93077, p-value = 3.655e-08
# Q-Q plots
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
qqnorm(df_primary$ai_use_composite, main = "Q-Q Plot: AI Use")
qqline(df_primary$ai_use_composite, col = "red")
qqnorm(df_primary$ai_disclosure_composite, main = "Q-Q Plot: AI Disclosure")
qqline(df_primary$ai_disclosure_composite, col = "red")

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
# Skewness and kurtosis for composites
cat("=== AI Use Composite ===\n")
## === AI Use Composite ===
cat("Skewness:", round(skewness(df_primary$ai_use_composite, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
## Skewness: -0.071
cat("Kurtosis:", round(kurtosis(df_primary$ai_use_composite, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
## Kurtosis: 2.547
cat("\n=== AI Disclosure Composite ===\n")
## 
## === AI Disclosure Composite ===
cat("Skewness:", round(skewness(df_primary$ai_disclosure_composite, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
## Skewness: 0.727
cat("Kurtosis:", round(kurtosis(df_primary$ai_disclosure_composite, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
## Kurtosis: 2.889

Manipulation Check

# mancheck1: 1=hierarchical[AR], 2=reciprocal[EM], 3=merit-based[MP]

mancheck_summary <- df_primary %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mc1_hierarchical = mean(mancheck1_1, na.rm = TRUE),
    mc1_reciprocal   = mean(mancheck1_2, na.rm = TRUE),
    mc1_merit        = mean(mancheck1_3, na.rm = TRUE),
    mc2_equals       = mean(mancheck2_1, na.rm = TRUE),
    mc2_power        = mean(mancheck2_2, na.rm = TRUE),
    mc2_evaluation   = mean(mancheck2_3, na.rm = TRUE)

Grouped bar chart - manipulation check means by condition and item

mancheck_long <- mancheck_summary %>%
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = c("AR", "EM", "MP"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -condition,
               names_to = "item",
               values_to = "mean") %>%
  mutate(
    check = case_when(
      item %in% c("mc1_hierarchical", "mc1_reciprocal", "mc1_merit") ~ "Policy Perception",
      TRUE ~ "Declaration Perception"
    ),
    item_label = case_when(
      item == "mc1_hierarchical" ~ "Hierarchical [AR]",
      item == "mc1_reciprocal"   ~ "Reciprocal [EM]",
      item == "mc1_merit"        ~ "Merit-based [MP]",
      item == "mc2_equals"       ~ "Equals [EM]",
      item == "mc2_power"        ~ "Institutional Power [AR]",
      item == "mc2_evaluation"   ~ "Evaluation [MP]"
    )
  )

  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~check, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("AR" = "#2196F3", "EM" = "#F44336", "MP" = "#4CAF50")) +

PRIMARY ANALYSIS

One-way ANOVA - Tests whether there are significant differences in means across the three

# relational framing conditions (AR, EM, MP) for intended AI use and disclosure
# Omnibus test - does not test specific pairwise differences
# Addresses RQ1 (AI use) and RQ2 (disclosure)

df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = c("AR", "EM", "MP")))

# RQ1: AI use across conditions
anova_use <- aov(ai_use_composite ~ condition, data = df_primary)
summary(anova_use)
##              Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value Pr(>F)
## condition     2   0.01  0.0068   0.008  0.992
## Residuals   198 158.99  0.8030
# RQ2: AI disclosure across conditions
anova_disclosure <- aov(ai_disclosure_composite ~ condition, data = df_primary)
summary(anova_disclosure)
##              Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value Pr(>F)  
## condition     2   6.21   3.106   2.824 0.0618 .
## Residuals   198 217.81   1.100                 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# Group means and SDs
df_primary %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_use        = mean(ai_use_composite, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_use          = sd(ai_use_composite, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_disclosure = mean(ai_disclosure_composite, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_disclosure   = sd(ai_disclosure_composite, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
## # A tibble: 3 × 5
##   condition mean_use sd_use mean_disclosure sd_disclosure
##   <fct>        <dbl>  <dbl>           <dbl>         <dbl>
## 1 AR            3.04  0.907            2.50          1.10
## 2 EM            3.02  0.825            2.12          1.00
## 3 MP            3.03  0.952            2.47          1.05

Tukey’s

# Only run for disclosure since AI use ANOVA was non-significant
tukey_disclosure <- TukeyHSD(anova_disclosure)
print(tukey_disclosure)

Bootstrapping

# 5000 samples to account for non-normal distribution of ai_disclosure
# AR as reference category (pre-registered)
boot_ar <- function(data, indices) {
  d <- data[indices, ]
  fit <- lm(ai_disclosure_composite ~ english_proficiency + uai + condition,
            data = d)
  return(coef(fit))
}

set.seed(123)
boot_ar_results <- boot(data = df_primary, statistic = boot_ar, R = 5000)

# CIs for each coefficient
boot.ci(boot_ar_results, type = "perc", index = 1) # intercept
## BOOTSTRAP CONFIDENCE INTERVAL CALCULATIONS
## Based on 5000 bootstrap replicates
## 
## CALL : 
## boot.ci(boot.out = boot_ar_results, type = "perc", index = 1)
## 
## Intervals : 
## Level     Percentile     
## 95%   ( 1.601,  5.979 )  
## Calculations and Intervals on Original Scale
boot.ci(boot_ar_results, type = "perc", index = 2) # english proficiency

# Mixed ANOVA for manipulation check - Policy Perception (mancheck1)
# Within-subject factor: relational dimension (hierarchical, reciprocal, merit)
# Between-subject factor: condition (AR, EM, MP)

library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

# Reshape to long format
mancheck_long_mixed <- df_primary %>%
  select(response_id, condition, mancheck1_1, mancheck1_2, mancheck1_3) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(mancheck1_1, mancheck1_2, mancheck1_3),
               names_to = "dimension",
               values_to = "rating") %>%
  mutate(dimension = case_when(
    dimension == "mancheck1_1" ~ "Hierarchical",
    dimension == "mancheck1_2" ~ "Reciprocal",
    dimension == "mancheck1_3" ~ "Merit-based"
  ))

# Mixed ANOVA
if (!requireNamespace("ez", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("ez", repos = "https://cran.rstudio.com/")
}
library(ez)
mixed_anova_mc1 <- ezANOVA(
  data = mancheck_long_mixed,
  dv = rating,
  wid = response_id,
  within = dimension,
  between = condition,
  type = 3,
  return_aov = TRUE
)
## Warning: Converting "response_id" to factor for ANOVA.
## Warning: Converting "dimension" to factor for ANOVA.
print(mixed_anova_mc1)

Hypothesis 3 - Disclosure gap - RQ3

# Composite gap = ai_use_composite - ai_disclosure_composite
# Item level gap = ai_use item - ai_disclosure item for each pair
# Positive gap = participants intend to use AI more than they disclose

df_primary <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(
    disclosure_gap_composite = ai_use_composite - ai_disclosure_composite,
    gap_1 = ai_use_1 - ai_disclosure_1, # brainstorming
    gap_2 = ai_use_2 - ai_disclosure_2, # literature review
    gap_3 = ai_use_3 - ai_disclosure_3, # rewriting
    gap_4 = ai_use_4 - ai_disclosure_4, # evaluating
    gap_5 = ai_use_5 - ai_disclosure_5, # writing parts
    gap_6 = ai_use_6 - ai_disclosure_6  # summarising
  )

# Composite gap summary
summary(df_primary$disclosure_gap_composite)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
## -3.5000  0.0000  0.6667  0.6683  1.5000  3.5000
# Item level gaps
item_gaps <- df_primary %>%
  summarise(
    brainstorming     = mean(gap_1, na.rm = TRUE),
    literature_review = mean(gap_2, na.rm = TRUE),
    rewriting         = mean(gap_3, na.rm = TRUE),
    evaluating        = mean(gap_4, na.rm = TRUE),
    writing_parts     = mean(gap_5, na.rm = TRUE),
    summarising       = mean(gap_6, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "mean_gap") %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_gap))

print(item_gaps)

USE-DISCLOSURE Gap Diagram

# Disclosure gap visualisations

# Data preparation
item_gap_data <- data.frame(
  item = c("Brainstorming", "Literature Review", "Rewriting", 
           "Evaluating", "Writing Parts", "Summarising"),
  ai_use = c(mean(df_primary$ai_use_1), mean(df_primary$ai_use_2),
             mean(df_primary$ai_use_3), mean(df_primary$ai_use_4),
             mean(df_primary$ai_use_5), mean(df_primary$ai_use_6)),
  ai_disclosure = c(mean(df_primary$ai_disclosure_1), mean(df_primary$ai_disclosure_2),
                    mean(df_primary$ai_disclosure_3), mean(df_primary$ai_disclosure_4),
                    mean(df_primary$ai_disclosure_5), mean(df_primary$ai_disclosure_6))
) %>%
  mutate(gap = ai_use - ai_disclosure) %>%
  arrange(desc(gap))

# 1. Paired bar chart
item_gap_long <- item_gap_data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(ai_use, ai_disclosure),
               names_to = "measure",
               values_to = "mean") %>%
  mutate(measure = case_when(
    measure == "ai_use" ~ "Intended AI Use",
    measure == "ai_disclosure" ~ "Intended Disclosure"
  ),
  item = factor(item, levels = item_gap_data$item))

ggplot(item_gap_long, aes(x = item, y = mean, fill = measure)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Intended AI Use" = "#2196F3", 
                                "Intended Disclosure" = "#F44336")) +
  labs(
    title = "Intended AI Use and Disclosure Intentions by Item",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean Score (1-5)",
    fill = NULL,
  ) +
 theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "top",
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5))

# 2. Dot plot with connecting lines
ggplot(item_gap_data, aes(y = reorder(item, gap))) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = ai_disclosure, xend = ai_use,
                   yend = reorder(item, gap)),
               colour = "grey70", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = ai_use, colour = "Intended AI Use"), size = 4) +
  geom_point(aes(x = ai_disclosure, colour = "Intended Disclosure"), size = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Intended AI Use" = "#2196F3",
                                  "Intended Disclosure" = "#F44336")) +
  labs(
    title = "Figure X. Intention-Disclosure Gap by Item",
    x = "Mean Score (1-5)",
    y = NULL,
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Items ordered by gap size. Lines connect intended AI use and intended disclosure means."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1, 5))

Effect sizes

# Cohen's f2 for regression models - Cohen (1988): small = .02, medium = .15, large = .35

library(effectsize)

# Cohen's f2 for regression models
# f2 = R2 / (1 - R2)
cat("=== Cohen's f2 - Model 1 AI Use ===\n")
## === Cohen's f2 - Model 1 AI Use ===
cat("f2 =", round(summary(model1_use)$r.squared /
                  (1 - summary(model1_use)$r.squared), 3), "\n")
## f2 = 0.007
cat("\n=== Cohen's f2 - Model 2 AI Use ===\n")
## 
## === Cohen's f2 - Model 2 AI Use ===

# Qualitative coding analysis
# Load data
qual_df <- read.csv("~/Desktop/ Qual Analysis.csv", 
                    header = FALSE,
                    col.names = c("condition", "ai_use_1", "ai_use_2", 
                                  "disclosure_1", "disclosure_2"))
# Clean
qual_df <- qual_df %>%
  filter(condition %in% c("AR", "EM", "MP")) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~trimws(tolower(.))))

# Check
cat("Total rows:", nrow(qual_df), "\n")
## Total rows: 201
table(qual_df$condition)
## 
## ar em mp 
## 67 67 67
# Define tasks
tasks <- c("brainstorming", "literature review", "evaluating", 
           "rewriting", "summarising", "writing parts")

# Overall AI use frequency
ai_use_all <- c(qual_df$ai_use_1, qual_df$ai_use_2)
ai_use_freq <- table(ai_use_all[ai_use_all %in% tasks])
cat("\n=== AI USE FREQUENCY ===\n")
## 
## === AI USE FREQUENCY ===
print(sort(ai_use_freq, decreasing = TRUE))
## 
##     brainstorming     writing parts literature review        evaluating 
##               163               125                50                33 
##         rewriting       summarising 
##                11                 6
# Overall disclosure frequency
disc_all <- c(qual_df$disclosure_1, qual_df$disclosure_2)
disc_freq <- table(disc_all[disc_all %in% tasks])
cat("\n=== DISCLOSURE FREQUENCY ===\n")
## 
## === DISCLOSURE FREQUENCY ===
print(sort(disc_freq, decreasing = TRUE))
## 
##     brainstorming        evaluating literature review         rewriting 
##               125                42                41                36 
##       summarising     writing parts 
##                23                 3
# Gap
cat("\n=== GAP (use - disclosure) ===\n")
## 
## === GAP (use - disclosure) ===
gap_df <- data.frame(
  task = tasks,
  ai_use = as.numeric(ai_use_freq[tasks]),
  disclosure = as.numeric(disc_freq[tasks])
) %>%
  mutate(
    ai_use = replace_na(ai_use, 0),
    disclosure = replace_na(disclosure, 0),
    gap = ai_use - disclosure
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(gap))
print(gap_df)

## 3 literature review     50         41   9
## 4        evaluating     33         42  -9
## 5       summarising      6         23 -17
## 6         rewriting     11         36 -25
#condition analysis
tasks <- c("brainstorming", "literature review", "evaluating", 
           "rewriting", "summarising", "writing parts")

for (cond in c("AR", "EM", "MP")) {
  cond_df <- qual_df %>% filter(condition == cond)
  cat("\n", cond, "— AI Use:\n")

  cat(cond, "— Disclosure:\n")
  cond_disc <- c(cond_df$disclosure_1, cond_df$disclosure_2)
  print(sort(table(cond_disc[cond_disc %in% tasks]), decreasing = TRUE))
}

#Sensitivity Analysis 1 - Full sample (n = 210)
df_full <- df %>%
  mutate(
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("AR", "EM", "MP")),
    ai_use_composite = rowMeans(select(., ai_use_1:ai_use_6), na.rm = TRUE),
    ai_disclosure_composite = rowMeans(select(., ai_disclosure_1:ai_disclosure_6), na.rm = TRUE),
    english_proficiency = case_when(
      b2q4 == 1 ~ 4,
      b2q4 == 2 ~ 3,

# Regression + bootstrapped CIs

                data = df_full)

## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = ai_disclosure_composite ~ english_proficiency + 
##     uai + condition, data = df_full)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -1.5239 -0.7699 -0.1891  0.6442  2.8968 
## 
## Coefficients:
##                      Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)          3.775957   0.992379   3.805 0.000188 ***
## english_proficiency -0.217575   0.211818  -1.027 0.305559    
## uai                 -0.010906   0.006146  -1.774 0.077504 .  
## conditionEM         -0.420744   0.177278  -2.373 0.018560 *  
## conditionMP         -0.001536   0.177979  -0.009 0.993121    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
##

##   (2 observations deleted due to missingness)
## Multiple R-squared:  0.04579,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.02698 
## F-statistic: 2.435 on 4 and 203 DF,  p-value: 0.04851
boot_sa1 <- function(data, indices) {
  d <- data[indices, ]
  fit <- lm(ai_disclosure_composite ~ english_proficiency + uai + condition, data = d)
  return(coef(fit))
}

set.seed(123)
boot_sa1_results <- boot(data = df_full, statistic = boot_sa1, R = 5000)

boot_sa3_results <- boot(data = df_sa3, statistic = boot_sa3, R = 5000)
boot.ci(boot_sa3_results, type = "perc", index = 4) # EM vs AR

                data = df_sa2)

# Sensitivity Analysis 3 - Manipulation check exclusions (n = 131)
df_sa3 <- df_primary %>%
  mutate(
    mancheck_fail = case_when(
      condition == "AR" & (mancheck1_1 < 3 | mancheck2_2 < 3) ~ TRUE,
      condition == "EM" & (mancheck1_2 < 3 | mancheck2_1 < 3) ~ TRUE,
      condition == "MP" & (mancheck1_3 < 3 | mancheck2_3 < 3) ~ TRUE,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(mancheck_fail == FALSE)

sa3_model <- lm(ai_disclosure_composite ~ english_proficiency + uai + condition,
                data = df_sa3)

Visualisations

# Visualisations

# 1. Bar chart of disclosure means by condition with error bars
disclosure_means <- df_primary %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(ai_disclosure_composite, na.rm = TRUE),
    se   = sd(ai_disclosure_composite, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n())
  )

ggplot(disclosure_means, aes(x = condition, y = mean, fill = condition)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), width = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("AR" = "#2196F3", "EM" = "#F44336", "MP" = "#4CAF50")) +
  labs(
    title = "Intended Disclosure by Relational Framing Condition",
    x = "Condition",
    y = "Mean Intended Disclosure (1-5)",
    caption = "Error bars represent standard error"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  ylim(0, 5)

RESULTS: English proficiency: 95% CI [-0.700, 0.222] — crosses zero, non-significant

UAI: 95% CI [-0.022, 0.002] — crosses zero, non-significant

EM vs AR: 95% CI [-0.644, 0.014] — just barely crosses zero, confirming the marginal result (p = .063)

MP vs AR: 95% CI [-0.195, 0.508] — crosses zero, non-significant

RESULTS - English proficiency: 95% CI [-0.700, 0.222] — crosses zero, non-significant

UAI: 95% CI [-0.022, 0.002] — crosses zero, non-significant

AR vs EM: 95% CI [-0.014, 0.644] — just barely crosses zero, confirming marginal result

MP vs EM: 95% CI [0.137, 0.815] — does not cross zero, confirms MP significantly higher than EM on disclosure

MP discloses significantly more than EM, and this holds under bootstrapping. AR vs EM remains marginal.

RESULTS: Composite gap — mean 0.81, median 0.67, range -2.67 to 3.83. Participants intend to use AI more than they disclose on average.

Evaluating writing: 1.12 — largest gap, Brainstorming: 0.95, Summarising without reading: 0.86, Literature review: 0.8, Rewriting: 0.73, Writing parts: 0.34 — smallest gap

CondiCondition-level ANOVA on disclosure gap

RESULTS: F(2, 199) = 2.546, p = .081. p = .081 means the disclosure gap does not significantly differ across the three conditions at α = .05.

There is a disclosure gap across all participants (mean = 0.81) — people intend to use AI more than they disclose. The gap is descriptively larger in EM than MP. But the gap does not significantly differ across conditions (F(2, 199) = 2.55, p = .081)
